name: Qwen3-TTS
tagline: Alibaba Qwen multilingual codec-LM TTS. Clones from a short reference with or without its transcript.

reference.recommended: One clean clip of 5 to 15 s with its exact transcript

options.label: bf16
options.help: Recommended on RTX GPUs. Half the VRAM of fp32.

options.label: fp16
options.help: For GPUs without bf16 support. Slightly higher risk of overflow.

options.label: fp32
options.help: Full precision. Twice the VRAM and slower. Forced on CPU.

help.summary: Weight and compute precision. Changing it reloads the model.
help.increase: fp32 is the most precise but uses twice the memory.
help.decrease: bf16 is the reference setting used by the Qwen team.

options.label: SDPA
options.help: PyTorch scaled-dot-product attention. Fast and available everywhere.

options.label: Eager
options.help: Plain implementation. Slowest, only for debugging.

options.label: FlashAttention 2
options.help: Fastest and lowest memory, but needs the flash-attn package, which is usually not installed on Windows.

help.summary: Attention implementation used by the language model. Changing it reloads the model.
help.increase: FlashAttention 2 saves VRAM on long inputs if it is installed.
help.decrease: Eager is the fallback when other kernels fail.
help.tip: SDPA is the right choice on Windows.

help.summary: Language of the text to speak. It selects the language token the model is conditioned on.
help.increase: Setting the exact language improves pronunciation and prevents accent drift.
help.decrease: Auto detects it from the text, which can fail on short or mixed-language text.
help.tip: Set English for English text. Japanese is handled by Irodori-TTS. The reference can be in another language (cross-lingual cloning).

options.label: Auto
options.help: ICL when every clip has a transcript, otherwise speaker embedding only.

options.label: ICL (with transcript)
options.help: The model reads the reference audio tokens and their transcript, then continues in the same voice. Best similarity, copies prosody and recording character.

options.label: Speaker embedding only
options.help: Uses only a speaker embedding (x-vector). No transcript needed, but similarity and naturalness are lower.

help.summary: How the reference voice is given to the model.
help.increase: ICL clones timbre, accent and speaking style closely but needs an exact transcript.
help.decrease: Speaker embedding only is quick to set up and robust to noisy references, but sounds less like the target.
help.tip: A wrong transcript hurts ICL badly. Type exactly what is said in the reference.

help.summary: How many takes to generate one after another. With Seed -1 every take gets its own random seed. With a fixed seed, take n uses seed + n - 1. Every take is reproducible on its own.
help.tip: Codec-LM models vary a lot between samples. 2 to 3 takes is a good habit.

help.summary: Random seed for sampling. -1 picks a new random seed for every take.
help.increase: A fixed value reproduces the same take with the same inputs and settings.
help.decrease: -1 gives a fresh variation every run.
help.tip: Copy the seed of a good take from the result card to keep it while you tune other settings.

help.summary: Randomness of the main (talker) token sampling, which decides rhythm, intonation and content timing.
help.increase: More expressive and varied, but more risk of slurring, repeats or strange pauses.
help.decrease: Flatter and more predictable. Too low can loop or sound monotone.
help.tip: 0.7 to 0.9 for narration. Lower it if takes are unstable.

help.summary: Only the k most likely tokens are considered at each step.
help.increase: Allows rarer choices, which adds variety and risk.
help.decrease: Restricts to safe choices. Very low values sound robotic.

help.summary: Nucleus sampling. Keeps the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities add up to p.
help.decrease: 0.8 to 0.95 trims unlikely tokens and makes takes more stable.
help.tip: Lower top-p is a gentle alternative to lowering temperature.

help.summary: Penalizes codec tokens that were already generated.
help.increase: Prevents stuck loops and endless syllables. Too high damages natural sustained sounds.
help.decrease: 1.0 disables it. More natural but loops can appear.
help.tip: Raise to 1.1 if a take loops or never stops.

help.summary: Upper limit of generated codec frames. The 12 Hz codec makes about 12.5 frames per second of audio. 0 uses the checkpoint value.
help.decrease: Caps runaway generations. Too low cuts the speech off.
help.tip: 1024 is about 80 s of audio, which is plenty for one paragraph.

help.summary: Whether the main token stream is sampled. Off means greedy decoding.
help.increase: On is required for natural speech.
help.decrease: Greedy decoding is deterministic but often repetitive or flat.

help.summary: Whether the sub-talker, which fills in the fine acoustic codebooks of every frame, samples or decodes greedily.
help.decrease: Off can sound buzzy or metallic.

help.summary: Randomness of the fine acoustic codebooks (timbre detail, breath, texture).
help.increase: More texture and breathiness, but more noise.
help.decrease: Cleaner but can sound dull or muffled.
help.tip: Change in small steps. 0.7 to 0.9 is safe.

help.summary: Top-k filter for the fine acoustic codebooks.
Nucleus filter for the fine acoustic codebooks.
help.decrease: Lower values suppress unlikely acoustic tokens, which can remove crackles.
